findings.reason: the predicate must be specified to recognise a record whose whole-document legacy fingerprint matches the current plan as covering all outstanding sections, or the legacy third form must synthesise section coverage, and a done-when must assert it, because §16's current done-when tests only the section-digest path.
findings.text: §16 states a stored review from before this change "carries no such key and is treated as covering no section, which the legacy whole-document form below keeps from forcing a re-review of an unchanged plan", but the described predicate joins `roadmap.implementable_sections` to "the union of section digests across every stored review", and a pre-change record contributes no section digests, so every outstanding section reads uncovered and the gate refuses an unchanged plan — the outcome §14's sidecar census exists to prevent

findings.reason: the plan must name the set's new home and add it to the `_plan_html.py` surface next to the tag expression, or the byte-identity test against the deleted parser cannot be written without a layering violation or a duplicate owner of the skip set.
findings.text: §16 makes `strip_tags` "definitional for the new digest" and requires it to drop "the interiors of the elements `_PROSE_SKIP_TAGS` names", but `_PROSE_SKIP_TAGS` is owned by `reckon/crew/plan_review.py` and §16 neither moves it to `reckon/_plan_html.py` nor names it beside `_TAG_RE` in the done-when grep, so the core-layer stripper would have to import a crew-layer constant (a core→crew layer inversion) or carry a second copy of the set

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — the section-keyed coverage predicate asserted in §16 cannot produce the outcome §16 claims for a pre-change stored record, so the module's contract leaks a decision to its callers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — `strip_tags` must reproduce the deleted parser's skip of `_PROSE_SKIP_TAGS`, a set owned by `reckon/crew/plan_review.py`, and §16 does not name where that set moves, so the core-layer stripper would import from the crew layer or duplicate it.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1478, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §16 adds one public definition (`strip_tags`) and §17 two (`plan_headings`, the machinery-element predicate), each naming in its own text why the public family cannot shrink (`structured_section_spans` and `landed_section_ids` keep external callers and are re-expressed, not removed; the `legacy` flag is retired from `plan_fingerprint`'s signature), and no CLI option, MCP view or refusal family is added.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — every mechanism §16/§17 adds names the existing owner it extends or re-homes: `_StructuredSectionSpanParser`/`structured_section_spans` (reckon/_plan_html.py:41,94), `_TAG_RE`/`count_open_decisions` (_plan_html.py:1506,1525), `section_record_id`/`section_id_candidates` (reckon/crew/routing.py:224,243), `landed_section_ids` (reckon/_store.py:1075), the `_store` heading helpers (_store.py:849-1106), `interface_counts` AST rules (reckon/interface_counts.py:97), `_RESOURCE_SEGMENT_RE`/`is_section_identity` (reckon/_schema.py), `roadmap.implementable_sections` and `recovery._plan_review_pending`; no subsystem is added without a cited owner.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — `strip_tags` (a public function over `_TAG_RE`) and the machinery-element predicate are not bare forwarders: `strip_tags` adds entity decoding, skip-tag interior removal and whitespace collapse, and the predicate centralises a `data-reckon` test that appears 14 times across 5 files; both state why they are public.
